text.p: South African fast bowler Allan Donald spearheaded a nine-wicket win for Warwickshire at Edgbaston on Saturday and plunged Sussex to the bottom of the county championship table.

Sussex veteran Bill Athey, 40 next month, fought a lost cause for three-and-a-quarter hours to delay Warwickshire's progress, grafting for 51 overs to make 67, but his only reward was to spare his county a third consecutive innings defeat.
Sussex, following on 164 behind, were eventually dismissed for 203, and Warwickshire quickly scored the required runs for the loss of one wicket to wrap up their fourth home win of the season.
Donald took four more wickets to claim overall figures of eight for 51 and medium-pacers Graeme Welch and Dougie Brown played the supporting roles with five wickets each.
Opener Jon Lewis, who joined Durham from Essex at the start of the season, hammered a career-best 160 not out to steer his new county to a rare victory against Derbyshire at Chester-le-Street.
Durham started the day at 48 for three needing a further 209 for victory, but won by six wickets after Lewis shared a stand of 204 with nightwatchman James Boiling, who made a championship best 62.
Lewis, whose 158 not out set up Durham's only other championship win of the season so far, against Kent in June, reached 1,008 first-class runs for the season.
